summary: This position paper proposes Structured Agentic Software Engineering, reframing software engineering around human agent coaches, autonomous software agents, and version-controlled collaboration artifacts.
why_it_matters: It is a strong roadmap paper for thinking beyond agentic coding toward disciplined, trustworthy agentic software engineering at team scale.
method_setup: The paper proposes a dual human-and-agent view of software engineering, introduces workbenches such as ACE and AEE, and defines artifacts and processes like BriefingScript, MentorScript, Consultation Request Packs, and Merge-Readiness Packs.
key_claims: Agentic software engineering needs structured processes, not just better prompts.
Humans should increasingly act as agent coaches and orchestrators rather than direct code producers.
Trustworthy agentic development depends on durable artifacts, review loops, and explicit governance.
limitations: It is a conceptual roadmap rather than a validated end-to-end engineering platform.
Many proposed artifacts and workflows still need empirical testing in real organizations.
